//: Per-repo settings for .claude/hooks. Copy to .claude/agent-config.json and keep only the keys you change. Every key is optional: a key you leave out keeps the default shown here, a key you set replaces its default whole (list the defaults you still want), and a malformed key falls back to its default with a warning. Keys starting with // are ignored. Paths are relative to the repo root and may not start with / or contain '..'. Installed as a plugin, the hooks run only in a repo that has this file (even {}) or .claude/agent-config-kit.lock.
//protectedBranches: Branches safety-check.sh and mcp-guard.sh never let an agent push to, delete, or write to through the GitHub MCP tools. A push is refused by refspec, by --all/--mirror, and by the checked-out branch when no destination is named. The user runs a real release push themselves with `! git push ...`.
//protectedPaths: What `rm -r` (and `git clean -f -- <path>`) may never take. A bare name (src) matches a folder or file of that name at any depth; a path with a slash (docs/adr) matches that path and everything under it. A folder git tracks files in, or that holds a repo, is protected whatever its name. Throwaways named zz-*, *-probe or __probe*, or ignored by git, that hold nothing git tracks, stay deletable.
//generatedPaths: Files or folders generated-guard.sh keeps agents from editing by hand (Write, Edit, MultiEdit and Serena's write tools, including a folder-wide replace_in_files). Change the source and run the generator instead. A path the repo does not have guards nothing.
//migrationsDirs: Folders of generated migrations migration-guard.sh keeps agents from editing by hand (drizzle-kit output, Alembic revisions). A folder the repo does not have guards nothing, so the hook switches itself off in a repo without migrations.
//commandWrappers: Commands that run another command, which safety-check.sh peels off before judging it: "name [subcommand ...] [-opt= ...]". The name and any listed subcommands are dropped, then the wrapper's options up to --; an option written with a trailing = takes the next word as its value. Example: "dotenvx run -f= --env-file=" makes `dotenvx run -f .env.local -- git push origin main` read as `git push origin main`. env, command, exec, nohup, time, sudo, nice, xargs and shells (bash -c) are always peeled.
//dbWriteGuard: db-guard.sh: toolPattern is a regex matched against the whole name of the production database's SQL tool. SQL that may write runs through it only while the user has unlocked db (docs/unlock.md). Wire db-guard.sh in settings.json with a matcher that covers the same tool. A malformed value falls back to the default.
//localePairs: Groups of files that change together, such as translation catalogues: when post-edit.sh sees one member edited while another has no change in the working tree or index, it tells the agent. Off by default. Example: [["messages/en.json", "messages/fr.json"]].
